title: Sets that are Cauchy in measure on every ball have a subsequence converging to a measurable set (parent steps 7–8)
statement: Let m ∈ ℕ and F_i ⊆ ℝ^m (i ∈ ℕ) be measurable. Assume that for every R > 0 and η > 0 there is N with L^m((F_i Δ F_j) ∩ B_R(0)) ≤ η for all i, j ≥ N. Then there are a strictly increasing σ : ℕ → ℕ and a measurable F' ⊆ ℝ^m such that L^m((F_{σ(i)} Δ F') ∩ B_R(0)) → 0 as i → ∞, for every R ∈ ℝ.
lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (F : ℕ → Set (Euclid m)), (∀ i, MeasurableSet (F i)) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ i j : ℕ, N ≤ i → N ≤ j → volume (symmDiff (F i) (F j) ∩ ball (0 : Euclid m) R) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal η) → ∃ (σ : ℕ → ℕ) (F' : Set (Euclid m)), StrictMono σ ∧ MeasurableSet F' ∧ ∀ R : ℝ, Tendsto (fun i => volume (symmDiff (F (σ i)) F' ∩ ball (0 : Euclid m) R)) atTop (𝓝 0)
